title_en: VMI Holland B.V. and Cooper (Kunshan) Tire Co., Ltd. v. Sachi Huachen Machinery (Suzhou) Co., Ltd. — dispute over confirmation of non-infringement of patent rights
ruling_gist_en: A patentee's request to the patent administrative department for handling a patent infringement dispute only against the user of the allegedly infringing product places the manufacturer and seller of the allegedly infringing product in a state of uncertainty regarding their business operations, and they are unable to participate in the administrative procedure to protect their rights and interests. Promptly determining whether the allegedly infringing product falls within the scope of protection of the patent in suit is in the interests of all parties involved and is conducive to saving administrative and judicial resources. It should be held that such a request for handling a patent infringement dispute constitutes a warning of patent infringement issued by the patentee, and the relevant party that was unable to participate in the administrative procedure has the right to file an action for confirmation of non-infringement of the patent right.

full_text_en:
VMI Holland B.V. and Cooper (Kunshan) Tire Co., Ltd. v. Sacchu Huachen Machinery (Suzhou) Co., Ltd. — dispute over confirmation of non-infringement of patent rights

[Ruling Summary]

Where a patentee files a request with the patent administrative department for handling a patent infringement dispute only against the user of the allegedly infringing product, resulting in the manufacturer and seller of the allegedly infringing product being in a state of uncertainty in their business operations, and where they cannot participate in the administrative handling procedure to protect their rights and interests, it is in the interests of all parties involved and conducive to saving administrative and judicial resources to determine as soon as possible whether the allegedly infringing product falls within the scope of protection of the patent in question. Such a request for handling a patent infringement dispute shall be deemed to constitute a warning of patent infringement issued by the patentee, and the relevant party that is unable to participate in the administrative handling procedure has the right to file a lawsuit for confirmation of non-infringement of the patent right.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2019) Zui Gao Fa Zhi Min Zhong No. 5

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): VMI Holland B.V. Domicile: Epe, the Kingdom of the Netherlands.

Legal Representative: Pieter Dirk Ramemaker, Special Projects Director of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Jiang Dafen, lawyer of Hui Ye (Nanjing) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Sun Qingmin, lawyer of Shanghai Hui Ye Law Firm.

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): Cooper (Kunshan) Tire Co., Ltd. Domicile: Bailing Road, Precision Science and Technology Park, Kunshan Development Zone, Jiangsu Province, the People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Yang Xun, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Liu Zhuan, lawyer of Hui Ye (Nanjing) Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Yongquan, lawyer of Beijing Shining Law Firm.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Sacchu Huachen Machinery (Suzhou) Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 12, Xinzhen Road, Zhoushi Town, Kunshan City, Jiangsu Province, the People's Republic of China.

Legal Representative: Zhang Yingzi, Chairman of the Company.

Agent ad litem: He Fang, lawyer of King & Wood Mallesons, Shanghai Office.

Agent ad litem: Sun Haoguang, lawyer of King & Wood Mallesons, Shanghai Office.

Appellant VMI Holland B.V. (hereinafter referred to as VMI) and Appellant Cooper (Kunshan) Tire Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Cooper), in their dispute with Respondent Sacchu Huachen Machinery (Suzhou) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Sacchu) over confirmation of non-infringement of patent rights, appealed against the civil ruling of the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court of Jiangsu Province (2018) Su 05 Min Chu No. 1453, and filed an appeal with this Court. After the case was docketed on April 2, 2019, this Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing on April 25, 2019. The agents ad litem of Appellant VMI, Jiang Dafen and Sun Qingmin, the agents ad litem of Appellant Cooper, Liu Zhuan and Liu Yongquan, and the agents ad litem of Respondent Sacchu, He Fang and Sun Haoguang, appeared in court. The case has now been concluded.

VMI and Cooper requested on appeal: 1. To set aside the ruling of the court of first instance. 2. To have the litigation costs borne by Respondent Sacchu. The main facts and reasons: 1. Sacchu's administrative complaint to the Intellectual Property Office constituted a warning of infringement within the meaning of the Patent Law, and the court of first instance erred in finding to the contrary; 2. Sacchu, knowing that the technical solution had been used by others earlier, still applied for a patent for it, and knowing that the product in question did not infringe, still maliciously filed an administrative complaint, which showed obvious bad faith and constituted an abuse of intellectual property rights, and the court of first instance erred in finding to the contrary; 3. The time point for filing a lawsuit should be based on the date of acceptance by the court, and the date of acceptance of the infringement lawsuit filed by Sacchu was more than one month after it received the warning letter, thus the action for confirmation of non-infringement filed by VMI and Cooper satisfied the conditions for filing; 4. The scope of the action for confirmation of non-infringement is broader than the scope of the infringement lawsuit filed by Sacchu, and the part of the action for confirmation of non-infringement exceeding that scope should not be dismissed; 5. Filing an action for confirmation of non-infringement is the statutory right of action of the plaintiffs, and it is necessary for the court to continue to hear the action for confirmation of non-infringement. During the second instance trial of this Court, the two appellants withdrew their second ground of appeal.

Sacchu argued in defense: 1. Sacchu never sent a warning letter, lawyer's letter, or other warning of infringement to either appellant, but directly filed an administrative complaint with the Intellectual Property Office in accordance with the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China and its Implementing Rules. Such an administrative complaint mechanism is a right conferred by Article 60 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China upon patentees to lawfully protect their rights and does not constitute a warning of infringement to the two appellants. Therefore, this case does not satisfy the conditions for accepting an action for confirmation of non-infringement; 2. Sacchu, within the period of the demand letter, had already initiated judicial proceedings in accordance with the law long before the two appellants submitted this lawsuit to the court of first instance, i.e., it filed an infringement lawsuit with the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court to resolve the dispute. Therefore, the two appellants clearly did not satisfy the statutory conditions for filing an action for confirmation of non-infringement; 3. The acceptance by the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court of the action for confirmation of non-infringement filed by the two appellants had obvious procedural defects.

VMI and Cooper requested in their claim before the court of first instance: 1. To confirm that VMI's manufacture, offer for sale, sale, import, and Cooper's use of the MAXX model passenger car radial tire building machine and related products did not infringe Sacchu's utility model patent No. ZL201420660550.1; 2. To have the litigation costs borne by Sacchu.

The court of first instance found the following facts: On May 24, 2018, the Suzhou Intellectual Property Office accepted a request filed by Sacchu for handling a dispute concerning Cooper's infringement of the patent in question. On June 12 of the same year, the Suzhou Intellectual Property Office transferred the administrative complaint to the Jiangsu Intellectual Property Office due to jurisdictional reasons. On July 5 of the same year, the Jiangsu Intellectual Property Office accepted Sacchu's request for handling the dispute concerning Cooper's infringement of the patent in question. On August 15 of the same year, the Jiangsu Intellectual Property Office issued a notice of suspension of processing, stating that because Cooper had filed a request with the Patent Reexamination Board of the China National Intellectual Property Administration (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Reexamination Board) for a declaration of invalidity of the patent in question and the request had been accepted, Cooper requested the Jiangsu Intellectual Property Office to suspend the processing, so the Jiangsu Intellectual Property Office decided to suspend the processing of the case. On September 24 of the same year, VMI sent a demand letter to Sacchu by mail. The demand letter stated that Sacchu had filed an administrative complaint for patent infringement with the Suzhou Intellectual Property Office, claiming that the MAXX model tire building machine used by Cooper and manufactured by VMI allegedly infringed a total of six patent rights of Sacchu, including the patent in question. Sacchu's administrative complaint had placed the production and operation of VMI and its Chinese customers in a highly unstable state. Therefore, Sacchu was required to withdraw the administrative complaint or file an infringement lawsuit in accordance with the law. Sacchu received the letter on September 26 of the same year. On September 30 of the same year, Sacchu replied to VMI. In the reply, Sacchu stated that it would not hesitate to file lawsuits or administrative complaints against any infringer, including Cooper and VMI, and that it had already done so. On October 19 of the same year, the court of first instance received the materials for a patent infringement lawsuit filed by Sacchu against VMI and Cooper for infringement of the patent in question. Sacchu requested an order that VMI and Cooper immediately cease the infringement, jointly and severally compensate Sacchu for economic losses of RMB 1,000,000, and bear the litigation costs. Sacchu remitted the litigation costs to the litigation cost account of the court of first instance on October 26 of the same year. The court of first instance docketed and accepted the patent infringement lawsuit on November 7 of the same year, with case number (2018) Su 05 Min Chu No. 1459. On October 29 of the same year, VMI and Cooper submitted the materials for an action for confirmation of non-infringement to the court of first instance. The case was docketed on November 7 of the same year, with case number (2018) Su 05 Min Chu No. 1453.

The court of first instance held that Article 18 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Patent Infringement Dispute Cases (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Law Judicial Interpretation) provides: "If the right holder sends a warning of patent infringement to another person, and the warned party or an interested party, after sending a written demand letter to the right holder to exercise its right to sue, and the right holder, within one month from the date of receipt of the written demand letter or within two months from the date of dispatch of the written demand letter, neither withdraws the warning nor files a lawsuit, and the warned party or interested party files a lawsuit with the people's court requesting confirmation that its conduct does not infringe the patent right, the people's court shall accept the case." This provision specifies the conditions for accepting an action for confirmation of non-infringement brought by the warned party or interested party: 1. The right holder issued a warning of infringement; 2. The warned party or interested party sent a written demand letter; 3. The right holder did not withdraw the warning or file a lawsuit within a reasonable period.

Regarding whether Sacchu's administrative complaint to the Intellectual Property Office constituted a "warning of infringement" within the meaning of the Patent Law, the court of first instance held that the Patent Law Judicial Interpretation does not clearly define "warning of infringement." Therefore, to correctly determine what constitutes a "warning of infringement," it is necessary to interpret it in light of the institutional purpose of the action for confirmation of non-infringement. In the context of patent law, a warning of infringement should refer to a situation where the right holder asserts infringement against the other party directly or indirectly, but is reluctant to resolve the dispute through legal procedures, thereby leaving the other party in a long-term state of uncertainty as to whether infringement exists. According to Article 60 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, both judicial protection and administrative protection are statutory forms of resolving intellectual property disputes. As long as the right holder's conduct is sufficient to create a factual dispute between it and the other party, and the right holder is reluctant to resort to statutory dispute resolution procedures, or, although having initiated administrative complaint procedures, due to the right holder's fault or reasons, the administrative complaint procedures fail to or are unable to make a definitive ruling on the disputed facts between the parties, thereby leaving the parties in a state of uncertainty regarding their legal relationship, it should be deemed to constitute a substantive warning of infringement to the other party.

Sacchu, believing that VMI and Cooper were allegedly infringing its patent rights, sought relief for its rights by directly filing a complaint with the Intellectual Property Office. The Intellectual Property Office accepted Sacchu's complaint for docketing and investigation, and organized specialized administrative law enforcement personnel to conduct an administrative investigation. The patent infringement dispute among Sacchu, VMI, and Cooper had entered a statutory dispute resolution procedure, and there was no evidence showing that Sacchu failed to cooperate or obstructed the normal progress of the administrative procedure. Therefore, VMI and Cooper could determine whether they constituted infringement through this administrative procedure. This method is fundamentally different from a "warning of infringement" within the meaning of the Patent Law. Even if the administrative investigation procedure was suspended due to Cooper's request to the Patent Reexamination Board for a declaration of invalidity of the patent in question, the cause and result of the suspension were not controlled or promoted by Sacchu. Regarding the original purpose and positioning of the action for confirmation of non-infringement, it is to curb the abuse of intellectual property rights and to safeguard and develop the parties' right to sue. Where Sacchu was lawfully exercising its statutory right to protect its rights without abusing its intellectual property rights, Sacchu's administrative complaint to the Intellectual Property Office did not constitute a "warning of infringement" within the meaning of the Patent Law.

Regarding the determination of the time point for "filing a lawsuit," the court of first instance held that the key to determining the time point for "filing a lawsuit" in the Patent Law Judicial Interpretation lies in correctly understanding the legislative rationale for establishing "filing a lawsuit" as one of the conditions for accepting an action for confirmation of non-infringement of intellectual property rights in China. The reason why the Patent Law Judicial Interpretation makes the right holder's failure to withdraw the warning or file a lawsuit within a reasonable period one of the conditions for accepting an action for confirmation of non-infringement is that the institutional positioning of the action for confirmation of non-infringement itself is to rescue the warned party or interested party from the unstable state of legal rights and obligations, to curb the right holder's abuse of intellectual property rights, and to achieve a balance of interests between the parties. This also determines that the action for confirmation of non-infringement is a supplementary remedy for the parties. If the right holder withdraws the warning or files a lawsuit within a reasonable period, the warned party or interested party has been rescued from the uncertain state and does not need to resolve the dispute between the parties through this system. Therefore, when the right holder files a lawsuit, requesting the people's court to make a judicial decision and requesting the public authority to exercise its public power to remedy its rights, the expression of intent to make a request to the people's court takes legal effect upon its arrival at the court, and it should be deemed that the right holder has actively asserted its rights. Therefore, "filing a lawsuit" here refers to the act of the right holder filing a lawsuit, not the act of the court accepting it. The time point for "filing a lawsuit" should be the time when the right holder asserts its rights by filing a lawsuit, not the time when the court accepts it. Sacchu submitted the materials for the lawsuit concerning the patent in question to the court of first instance on October 19, 2018, and prepaid the case acceptance fee on October 26. Both of these time points were within one month after Sacchu received the demand letter. It can be seen that Sacchu, within one month after receiving the demand letter, actively sought relief from the people's court for its rights, and its expression of intent was clear and timely. Therefore, where the right holder actively exercised its rights and initiated litigation proceedings within a reasonable period, VMI and Cooper should not file an action for confirmation of non-infringement regarding the same legal relationship.

Therefore, even if Sacchu had issued a warning of infringement, based on the fact that Sacchu filed a lawsuit within a reasonable period, the conditions for accepting an action for confirmation of non-infringement were not satisfied, and the claims of VMI and Cooper should be dismissed. At the same time, given that VMI and Cooper had filed an action for confirmation of non-infringement, from the perspective of protecting the rights and interests of both parties and improving trial efficiency, in the infringement lawsuit, the court would, depending on the circumstances, subject Sacchu's right to withdraw the lawsuit to a certain degree of review or restriction.

In conclusion, the court of first instance ruled: to dismiss the claims of VMI and Cooper.

During the second instance trial, VMI submitted the following six new pieces of evidence to this Court:

1. Sacchu's administrative complaint, the Suzhou Intellectual Property Office's Notice of Reply, the Notice of Composition of the Collegial Panel, the Notice of Evidence Submission, and a Statement of the On-site Inspection by the Suzhou Intellectual Property Administrative Law Enforcement Detachment;
2. Sacchu's administrative complaint, the service receipt of the Jiangsu Intellectual Property Office, the Notice of Reply, the Notice of Evidence Submission, the Notice of Acceptance of the Administrative Complaint, and the inspection record;
3. The Jiangsu Intellectual Property Office's Notice of Case Closure Su Zhi Fa Chu Zi (2018) No. 9 and the service receipt;

The purpose of evidence 1-3 above is to prove: the administrative complaint filed by the respondent never named VMI as a requested party; the respondent requested the Intellectual Property Office to order the user to cease using the allegedly infringing product; the administrative complaint filed by the respondent actually affected the appellants and left the issue of whether the appellants constituted infringement in a state of uncertainty.

4. Sacchu's application for pre-litigation evidence preservation, the civil rulings of the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court (2018) Su 05 Zheng Bao No. 56-57, and the service documents of the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court;
5. Sacchu's complaint (case numbers (2018) Su 05 Min Chu No. 1095-1096) and the service documents of the Suzhou Intermediate People's Court;

The purpose of evidence 4-5 above is to prove: despite Cooper having twice cooperated with administrative law enforcement personnel for on-site inspections, the respondent still initiated litigation proceedings; the respondent did not treat the administrative complaint procedure as a judicial procedure for dispute resolution, but instead repeatedly filed administrative complaints and infringement lawsuits to continuously disrupt the normal production and operation of the appellants; in order to avoid being in an extremely uncertain state in production and operation, the appellants' sending of the demand letter was entirely consistent with the original purpose of the system for confirming non-infringement.

6. VMI's application for an increase in the claims and the mailing receipt, the purpose of which is to prove that the scope of the claims in this action for confirmation of non-infringement is broader than that of the corresponding positive action, and at least the part of the claims exceeding that scope should not be dismissed; the court of first instance did not rule on the appellants' application for an increase in the claims, which was a procedural violation.

Cooper recognized the authenticity, legality, relevance, and the purpose of proof of all evidence submitted by VMI.

Sacchu recognized the authenticity and legality of the evidence submitted by VMI, but did not recognize its relevance or purpose of proof.

This Court's authentication opinion: the Statement of On-site Inspection in evidence 1 above was already evidence in the first instance, therefore it is not new evidence in the second instance; the patents involved in evidence 4 and 5 are not the patent in question in this case and are irrelevant to this case, therefore they are not new evidence in the second instance. This Court confirms the authenticity, legality, and relevance of the remaining evidence submitted by VMI, but whether it can achieve its purpose of proof will be comprehensively determined in the context of the entire case.

Cooper and Sacchu did not submit new evidence to this Court.

This Court found during trial that the facts found by the court of first instance were basically accurate. This Court also found: 1. Sacchu's request in the administrative handling was for an order that Cooper cease the acts of infringing the patent in question, including but not limited to ceasing the use of the tire building machine model MAXX; 2. On July 12, 2018, the Jiangsu Intellectual Property Office went to Cooper to conduct an on-site inspection of the tire building machine model MAXX; 3. On December 18, 2018, Sacchu withdrew its request for handling the patent infringement dispute from the Jiangsu Intellectual Property Office; 4. On January 16, 2019, VMI sent an application for an increase in the claims to the court of first instance, requesting confirmation that the VMI245 fully automatic one-step tire building machine did not infringe the patent in question. Upon verification by this Court, the court of first instance had received the aforementioned application for an increase in the claims.

This Court holds that there are three main issues of dispute in the second instance: First, whether Sacchu's request for handling the patent infringement dispute constituted a warning of infringement within the meaning of the Patent Law; Second, how to determine the time when Sacchu filed the infringement lawsuit; Third, whether the claims in the action for confirmation of non-infringement filed by the appellants exceeded the scope of the request for handling the patent infringement dispute.

I. Whether Sacchu's request for handling the patent infringement dispute constituted a warning of infringement within the meaning of the Patent Law

Opinion of the Court

This Court holds that when a right holder claims that the opposing party has infringed its rights but fails to resolve the matter through legal procedures, leaving the opposing party in a state of uncertainty, the purpose of the action for a declaration of non-infringement is to grant the opposing party the right to sue, providing a means to eliminate this uncertainty. In an action for a declaration of non-infringement of a patent, the scope of trial is to determine whether the technical solution implemented by the plaintiff falls within the protection scope of the defendant's patent rights, and its purpose is also to eliminate the plaintiff's uncertainty as to whether the technical solution it implements falls within the protection scope of another person's patent rights, thereby facilitating its business decisions. In a patent infringement dispute, the patentee has a certain degree of choice as to whether the dispute is handled by the patent administrative department or tried by a people's court. However, regardless of whether the dispute is handled by the patent administrative department or tried by a people's court, the key lies in determining whether the accused infringing product or method falls within the protection scope of the patent in question.

First, in this case, Sachi Company filed a request with the patent administrative department to handle a patent infringement dispute, indicating that it believed that the tire building machine of model MAXX involved in the case infringed its patent in question. Although the opposing party in this administrative procedure was Cooper Company, the user of the accused infringing equipment, for VMI Company, the producer of equipment of this model, it must have recognized that the equipment it produced and sold might be subject to infringement accusations. Once the dispute handling authority determines that infringement has been established, its equipment market will inevitably be affected. Therefore, in this case, the impact of the administrative procedure on VMI Company's operations is objectively existing.

Second, in the request for handling a patent infringement dispute filed by Sachi Company, the only requested party was Cooper Company, the user of the equipment, while VMI Company, the manufacturer of the equipment, was not a requested party. VMI Company had no opportunity to participate in the administrative procedure and could not assert its corresponding rights in that administrative procedure. For VMI Company, whether the accused infringing equipment it manufactures and sells would be found to constitute infringement by the patent administrative department had become a state of uncertainty, its product sales market might be affected as a result, and its rights and interests could not be safeguarded in the corresponding administrative procedure. The purpose of VMI Company in filing this action for a declaration of non-infringement of a patent is to promptly confirm through judicial proceedings that the MAXX model tire building machine it produces and sells does not fall within the protection scope of Sachi Company's patent in question, thereby extricating itself from the uncertain state of possibly facing infringement accusations and stabilizing its corresponding market. In any event, promptly determining whether the MAXX model tire building machine falls within the protection scope of Sachi Company's patent in question serves the interests of all parties involved in this case and is also conducive to saving administrative and judicial resources. In this case, the right holder requested the patent administrative department to handle a patent infringement dispute, and the outcome of such handling may directly affect the interests of VMI Company, which was not a requested party. It can be considered that VMI Company has already received an infringement warning. Therefore, in this case, as far as VMI Company is concerned, the request for handling a patent infringement dispute filed by Sachi Company should be regarded as an infringement warning within the meaning of Article 18 of the Judicial Interpretation of the Patent Law. VMI Company's ground of appeal that Sachi Company's request for handling a patent infringement dispute constitutes an infringement warning is reasonable. The original trial court's application of law was improper, and this Court hereby corrects it. Furthermore, whether the patentee has abused its rights is not a prerequisite for determining whether its conduct constitutes an infringement warning. The action for a declaration of non-infringement itself does not address the issue of whether the patentee has abused its rights. The original trial court did not make a separate determination on whether Sachi Company abused its intellectual property rights. Therefore, the ground of appeal of VMI Company and Cooper Company that the original trial court's failure to determine that Sachi Company abused its intellectual property rights constitutes an error in fact finding cannot be sustained.

II. How the Time When Sachi Company Filed the Infringement Action Should Be Determined

An action for a declaration of non-infringement of a patent and a patent infringement action within the same scope essentially both address whether the technical solution implemented by the alleged infringer falls within the protection scope of the patent in question. If a patent infringement action is filed first, the opposing party can raise a non-infringement defense, and there is no need for a corresponding action for a declaration of non-infringement. The failure of the patentee to withdraw the warning or file an action within a reasonable period is one of the conditions for accepting an action for a declaration of non-infringement of a patent. If the right holder withdraws the warning or files an action within a reasonable period, the warned party or interested party is relieved from the uncertain state, or the dispute can be resolved in the patent infringement action, eliminating the need to resolve the dispute through an action for a declaration of non-infringement.

In this case, the original trial court received the prosecution materials submitted by Sachi Company on October 19, 2018, and Sachi Company also prepaid the case acceptance fee on the 26th of the same month. The time when Sachi Company filed the infringement action can be determined as October 19, 2018. This point in time was still within two months from the date VMI Company sent the letter of demand and within one month from the date Sachi Company received the letter of demand. Therefore, although Sachi Company's request to the patent administrative department to handle the infringement dispute in this case constitutes an infringement warning, as the patentee, Sachi Company had filed an infringement action within a reasonable period. The action for a declaration of non-infringement of a patent filed by VMI Company and Cooper Company in this case does not satisfy the corresponding acceptance conditions stipulated in the Judicial Interpretation of the Patent Law. In summary, the ground of appeal of VMI Company and Cooper Company that the time when Sachi Company filed the action should be based on the date the court accepted the case and that the action for a declaration of non-infringement should exist independently cannot be sustained.

III. Whether the Claim in This Action for a Declaration of Non-Infringement of a Patent Extends Beyond the Scope of the Request for Handling the Patent Infringement Dispute

According to the purpose of the system of an action for a declaration of non-infringement of a patent, the scope of the claim for declaration should not exceed the scope of the right holder's infringement warning; otherwise, it would be groundless. That is, the patentee's infringement warning is the basic prerequisite for the opposing party to file an action for a declaration of non-infringement. Any claims of the opposing party that exceed the scope of the patentee's infringement warning should not be included in the trial scope of the action for a declaration of non-infringement.

In the second instance of this case, all parties confirmed that the MAXX model tire building machine and the VMI245 fully automatic one-step tire building machine in VMI Company's application for increasing claims are different pieces of equipment. In this case, Sachi Company's request for handling a patent infringement dispute only involved the MAXX model tire building machine. The use of the phrase "including but not limited to" does not mean that the matters requested for handling can be infinitely extended to other equipment. Moreover, the relevant patent administrative department only conducted corresponding handling procedures for the MAXX model tire building machine, which means that Sachi Company's infringement warning was only directed at the MAXX model tire building machine. A party cannot file an action for a declaration of non-infringement that exceeds the scope of the infringement warning. Therefore, the increased claims of VMI Company should not be addressed in this case. If VMI Company believes that its VMI245 fully automatic one-step tire building machine has received other infringement warnings, it may seek relief separately. Accordingly, this Court does not uphold the ground of appeal of VMI Company and Cooper Company that their increased claims should not be dismissed and that the original trial court violated legal procedures.

In summary, the facts found in the original ruling are basically clear. This Court has corrected the improper application of law, which does not affect the result of the ruling. Therefore, this Court does not uphold the appeal requests of VMI Company and Cooper Company. Pursuant to Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 334 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ruled as follows:

The appeal is dismissed, and the original ruling is affirmed. This ruling is final.
